proposal: The Mandate recommends that DOL prohibit ERISA plan investing based on factors unrelated to investor risk and return and return to the first Trump Administration's approach of permitting only pecuniary factors, while still allowing legitimate non-ESG factors such as governance or domestic supply chains. It also suggests considering greater scrutiny of plan investments in China.

status_summary: DOL has announced a replacement rulemaking and, per trade press, sent the draft to White House review, but no proposal had been published in the Federal Register as of 2026-10-15. On 2025-04-21 DOL told the Fifth Circuit it would reconsider the 2022 investment-duties rule (which allows ESG factors as tiebreakers), and on 2025-05-28 it said it would pursue new rulemaking. The regulatory agenda lists RIN 1210-AC37, Prudence and Loyalty in Selecting Plan Investments and Exercising Shareholder Rights, which would revise 29 CFR 2550.404a-1 so fiduciaries choose investments and vote shares based only on financial considerations; trade press reported that DOL's Employee Benefits Security Administration submitted a draft of that rule to the Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs on 2026-06-30. The 2022 rule therefore remains in effect, and DOL's separate 2026-03-31 proposal on selecting investment alternatives does not address ESG.

timeline.event: In Utah v. Micone (N.D. Tex.), the district court grants summary judgment to the defendants and upholds the 2022 rule, per a case tracker; the case is the one on appeal to the Fifth Circuit.

In the Fifth Circuit appeal over the 2022 rule (Utah v. Chavez-DeRemer, formerly Utah v. Walsh), DOL asks to hold the case in abeyance, saying it intends to reconsider the rule, including whether to rescind it; the court grants only a 30-day pause on 2025-04-28.
DOL tells the Fifth Circuit it will engage in new rulemaking on the subject of the challenged 2022 rule, to appear in the spring regulatory agenda.

Adjacent action, not on ESG: DOL's Employee Benefits Security Administration proposes a regulation and safe harbor on the duty of prudence in choosing designated investment alternatives, including funds with alternative assets, implementing Executive Order 14330; comments closed 2026-06-01. The portions read did not discuss ESG or the 2022 rule.

DOL's Employee Benefits Security Administration sends a draft rule titled Prudence and Loyalty in Selecting Plan Investments and Exercising Shareholder Rights to the White House Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs for review, per trade press reports; the draft is not published and no review conclusion was reported.

The Federal Register publishes the introduction to the 2026 Unified Agenda, which includes the DOL entry titled Prudence and Loyalty in Selecting Plan Investments and Exercising Shareholder Rights at the proposed-rule stage.

title: Remove ESG factors from ERISA plan investing and limit fiduciaries to pecuniary factors
